Edit this transparent apartment floor-and-fixed-fixtures PNG. Keep exact 1536x1024 canvas, original camera and every object's coordinates. Remove that tiled WALL strip completely; the layer must contain no vertical wall or backsplash anywhere. Preserve the toilet, sink, plumbing, shower/tub, washer/dryer, kitchen counter, all wooden and tiled horizontal floors, lighting, texture and transparency exactly. No other edits, no new objects, no backdrop or exterior pixels; genuinely transparent RGBA outside the apartment.

Use case: background-extraction / precise-object-edit.
Input 1 is the approved Brick walk-up apartment. Input 2 is its floor-and-fixed-fixtures layer, supplied ONLY to establish registration.
Create a SINGLE WALLS-ONLY transparent RGBA PNG sprite for overlaying input 2. Full canvas exactly 1536x1024. Preserve the original source's identical wall XY coordinates, camera, angle, scale, crop, and composition. No recentering, enlarging, cropping to visible objects, exploded layout, new walls, or floorplan redesign.
Retain ONLY existing exterior and interior walls, foreground facade, wall caps, doors and doorframes, window frames, attached wall lights and wall-mounted closet rail/cabinets. Keep the same source brick/plaster textures and condition. There is NO roof.
Remove EVERY FLOOR PIXEL, all horizontal wooden/tiled floor surfaces, all exterior scenery, all ground/pavement/plants/background, all furniture, laptop, kitchen sink counter/lower cabinets, toilet, bathroom sink, tub/shower/curtain and washer/dryer. Those fixtures belong ONLY to the other layer. At the original fixture silhouettes make transparent holes rather than painting wall over the fixtures; this overlay must reveal the fixed fixtures beneath. Through windows, between walls, through doors, and in every former room-floor area must be genuinely alpha-zero transparency, not a painted black or white fill or fake checkerboard. Do not leave glimpses of the old wood floor visible in windows.
The image should look like the original empty apartment's freestanding wall skeleton floating over transparent nothing, with the original room arrangement and all wall pieces still exactly in place. No floor slab, ground shadow, foundation platform, new scenery, text, labels, people or border. This is an overlay layer, NOT a complete apartment illustration.
